canonical_name: MMLU-Redux (Gema et al., 'Are We Done with MMLU?'; v1.0 3,000 Qs/30 subjects, v2.0 5,700 Qs/57 subjects)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04127v1 (v1 6 Jun 2024: 'a subset of 3,000 manually re-annotated questions across 30 MMLU subjects'; dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/edinburgh-dawg/mmlu-redux)
metric: accuracy (exact match on 4-option MC, zero-shot as in ZeroEval/lab usage)
ab_mode: zero-shot, single run (API default decoding), ZeroEval prompt; 2,778 error-free MMLU-Redux 1.0 items
score_at_release: n/a (creators reported only per-subject before/after accuracies, no aggregate); first aggregate public results: GPT-4o-2024-05-13 88.01 on ZeroEval (2024-07-13)
lineage: parent: MMLU (2020-09); MMLU-Redux 1.0 (2024-06) -> MMLU-Redux 2.0 (arXiv v3 2025-01, 5,700 Qs, all 57 subjects; HF edinburgh-dawg/mmlu-redux-2.0); siblings MMLU-Pro (2024-06), MMMLU (2024-09)
notes: Creators report no human baseline -> B (90). Caller's MMLU expert estimate 89.8 (Hendrycks et al.) was not measured on this split; applying it as an A threshold gives the identical event (no public result between 89.8 and 92.84 before 2024-09; top before was GPT-4o 88.26/chatgpt-4o-latest 88.88 on ZeroEval). ZeroEval (independent, AI2/Yuchen Lin) leaderboard began 2024-07-13 (GPT-4o 88.01 top); o1-mini 86.72 added 2024-09-13; o1-preview 92.84 added 2024-09-15. First lab self-report >=90: DeepSeek-R1 92.9 (2025-01-20). Version issue: v2.0 (Jan 2025) adds 2,700 items (>10% change) and could be a separate unit; coded here as one unit because the event (2024-09) predates v2.0; first >=90 results specifically on v2.0 not separately verified. Lab raw names 'MMLU-redux-2.0' refer to v2.0.

canonical_name: MMMLU (OpenAI Multilingual MMLU: MMLU test set professionally translated into 14 languages)
release_source: https://github.com/openai/simple-evals/blob/main/multilingual_mmlu_benchmark_results.md (commit 01c488b, 2024-09-11 'Add Multilingual MMLU repro code and results'); HF dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/MMMLU createdAt 2024-09-13
metric: accuracy, averaged over the 14 non-English languages (0-shot CoT in simple-evals)
strict_system: GPT-5.1 (scored by Google DeepMind via official OpenAI API, i.e., independent run)
strict_source: https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_3_pro_model_evaluation.pdf ('Google DeepMind calculated the following scores using official provider APIs ... MMMLU'); GPT-5.1 91.0% per https://www.vellum.ai/blog/google-gemini-3-benchmarks
score_at_release: 86.7 (mean of 14 per-language scores computed by coder; OpenAI listed per-language only, English 90.8 excluded)
lineage: parent: MMLU (2020-09); siblings: earlier lab-internal machine-translated 'Multilingual MMLU' (Anthropic Claude 3, 2024-03; Meta Llama 3.1, 2024-07) are different datasets; Global-MMLU (2024-12), MMLU-ProX (2025-03) later multilingual successors
best_by_cutoff: 92.7, Claude Mythos Preview (avg 5 trials), 2026-04-07, Anthropic system card (per lab_reports; llm-stats.com/benchmarks/mmmlu top entry 0.927); Gemini 3.1 Pro 92.6 (2026-02-19, https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/pro/)
notes: No creator human baseline -> B (90). Caller's MMLU 89.8 expert estimate would not change the event (no result in [89.8,90) before 2025-11: GPT-5-thinking 89.4 computed from per-language table in GPT-5 system card 2025-08; Claude Opus 4.1 89.5 2025-08; o3-high 88.8 in simple-evals 2025-04; Gemini 2.5 Pro 89.5 in Google's Nov-2025 table). Same-day 2025-11-18 table also lists GPT-5.1 91.0 (computed by Google DeepMind). Pre-2024-09 'Multilingual MMLU' lab lines (Claude 3 Opus 79.1, Llama 3.1 83.2) are different internal translations, not this benchmark. DeepSeek/Qwen 'MMMLU' base-model 5-shot numbers are a different protocol. Metric averages exclude English.

canonical_name: OpenAI-MRCR (openai/mrcr; Multi-Round Co-reference Resolution, public re-implementation of Google's internal MRCR); bug-fixed release Dec 2025 = 'OpenAI MRCR v2'
metric: mean SequenceMatcher match ratio; coded config = 2-needle, 128K bin (creators' headline 'OpenAI-MRCR: 2 needle 128k' at release)
strict_system: not established (no independent/organizer-verified >=90 at 2-needle 128k found; Context Arena data not accessible)
n_items: 2400 (2/4/8 needles x 8 context bins 4K-1M x 100 samples)
lineage: parent: Google MRCR (Gemini 1.5 report 2024-05; Michelangelo arXiv 2409.12640, 2024-09) and Google MRCR v2 8-needle (2025-06) - both internal ('MRCR v2 which is not publicly available yet', Gemini 3 Pro eval PDF Nov 2025); OpenAI-MRCR (2025-04) -> bug-fix 2025-12-05 (~10% items had too many needles, ~5% wrong ground truth) reported as 'OpenAI MRCR v2' from GPT-5.2 (2025-12)
best_by_cutoff: 2-needle 128k: 95.2 GPT-5 (2025-08-07, OpenAI). 8-needle (v2): 100.0 GPT-6 Astra at 256K-512K (2026-09-03, OpenAI blog per lab_reports, unverified)
notes: HARD CALL (unit ambiguity + parametric config). Unit 'MRCR' mixes (a) Google's internal MRCR/MRCR v2 (GDM-MRCR; Google 128k-average numbers e.g. Gemini 2.5 Pro 03-25 94.5% are on a non-public set -> would be excluded:internal) and (b) OpenAI's public openai/mrcr; coded (b). Config: no official aggregate; used creators' release headline (2-needle 128k). Pre-GPT-5 best at 128k: Gemini 2.5 Pro 76.8, MiniMax-M1-40k 76.1, o3 56.5 (MiniMax-M1 report arXiv 2506.13585, 2025-06). Under the harder 8-needle config the outcome differs: 8-needle 4K-8K already 98.2 (GPT-5.2, 2025-12); 8-needle 256K bin >=90 first at Claude Sonnet 4.6 90.6 (2026-02, per lab_reports, unverified) / GPT-5.6 91.5 at 256K-512K (2026-07); 8-needle 1M still <90 (Opus 4.6 76.0, DeepSeek-V4-Pro 83.5) -> alive under 1M config. Dec-2025 bug fix touched ~10-15% of items (borderline new unit). Caveat: Context Arena (independent OpenAI-MRCR leaderboard, launched 2025-04) could hold an earlier >=90 2-needle-128k result (e.g., Grok 4, 2025-07) - not checkable (JS site, search budget exhausted).

canonical_name: MT-Bench (LMSYS; Zheng et al., 'Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena')
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685 (v1 2023-06-09); code/questions released in FastChat commit b494d0c 2023-06-16 'Release MT-bench code' (https://github.com/lm-sys/FastChat/tree/main/fastchat/llm_judge)
metric: mean GPT-4 single-answer grade (1-10) over 80 questions x 2 turns
ab_mode: standard MT-Bench single-answer grading, GPT-4 judge
ab_source: https://huggingface.co/spaces/lmsys/chatbot-arena-leaderboard/blob/main/leaderboard_table_20231116.csv (first table with an MT-bench value >=9.0; tables 20230619-20231108 max = GPT-4 8.99)
lineage: successors by same team: Arena-Hard-Auto v0.1 (2024-04-19 blog; arXiv 2406.11939) -> Arena-Hard v2; derivatives by others: MT-Bench-101 (2024-02), Mistral MM-MT-Bench (2024-09, multimodal); 'CMT-Benchmark' and 'MMT-Bench' in lab lines are unrelated benchmarks
best_by_cutoff: 9.35, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, 2024-09-19, https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/qwen2.5-llm/ (self-report; official LMSYS table max stays 9.32 GPT-4-1106-preview through leaderboard_table_20250804.csv)
notes: Scale 1-10 per caller (max 10) -> B threshold 9.0; no human-answer baseline (paper measures human-judge agreement only). GPT-4 at release 8.99 (just under). GPT-4-0613 9.18 appears in table 20231206. Possible C (not coded): LMSYS stopped scoring new models on MT-bench in early 2024 (no MT-bench for Claude 3 / Llama 3 in leaderboard_table_20240501.csv) and launched Arena-Hard-Auto as a more separable replacement (blog 2024-04-19: 'Arena Hard Auto v0.1 offers significantly stronger separability against MT Bench'; paper intro: existing benchmarks 'becoming saturated and unable to differentiate between state-of-the-art models'), but no explicit deprecation/saturation statement about MT-Bench itself. Lab variants with GPT-4o judge (Mistral 2024) are non-standard protocol.

canonical_name: MakeMePay (openai/evals make-me-pay; con-artist vs simulated mark, OpenAI 'Contextual' variant with GPT-4o mark)
metric: % of conversations in which the con-artist receives a payment (donation_success_rate); secondary: % dollar extraction
abandoned_evidence: Last lab report: GPT-4.5 system card 2025-02-27 (https://cdn.openai.com/gpt-4-5-system-card-2272025.pdf, 57% payments); no reports by any of the 9 labs through 2026-09-30 (19 months); no public leaderboard. OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2 (2025-04-15, https://openai.com/index/updating-our-preparedness-framework/): 'Persuasion risks will be handled outside the Preparedness Framework'.
score_at_release: n/a (no results published with the eval in 2023-09; first published results in o1-preview system card 2024-09-12)
n_items: n/a (interactive; configurable number of simulated conversations, mark prompt variants guarded/balanced/generous)
lineage: sibling: MakeMeSay (same openai/evals release 2023-09); OpenAI 'Contextual' variant used in system cards 2024-09..2025-02 with mark fixed as GPT-4o
best_by_cutoff: 79% payments (9% dollar extraction), o3-mini (pre-mitigation), 2025-01-31, https://cdn.openai.com/o3-mini-system-card-feb10.pdf ('o3-mini (Pre-Mitigation) receives the most payments (79%)')
notes: HARD CALL on stratum: score is a success rate against a reference 'mark' model (repo default gpt-4-32k; GPT-4o fixed in all OpenAI system-card runs), so ceiling is bounded (100%) but defined relative to the mark; coded main because the reference was fixed across all 5 lab reports; alternative coding excluded:no_ceiling (win rate vs changeable reference / $ extracted). Pre- and post-mitigation results reported; post-mitigation partly reflects refusal propensity. Inconsistency: GPT-4.5 card says 'GPT-4.5 scores the highest (57%) at receiving payments' while o3-mini card reported o3-mini pre-mitigation 79% (different run/checkpoint). Only OpenAI reports it (5 releases).

canonical_name: MakeMeSay (openai/evals make-me-say; manipulator must get simulated human to say a codeword; OpenAI 'Contextual' variant with GPT-4o manipulatee)
metric: manipulator win rate (% of games where manipulatee says the codeword without guessing it)
score_at_release: n/a (no results published with the eval in 2023-09; first published results in o1-preview system card 2024-09-12)
n_items: n/a (interactive games; codeword lists easy/medium/hard/very-hard, default medium-and-hard)
lineage: adapted from a Google DeepMind methodology (Phuong, Krakovna et al., per openai/evals readme); sibling MakeMePay (2023-09); xAI variant from Grok 4 card (2025-07/08): defender = non-reasoning Grok 3 Mini, 15 turns
best_by_cutoff: 73%, o3-mini (pre-mitigation), 2025-01-31, https://cdn.openai.com/o3-mini-system-card-feb10.pdf ('o3-mini (Pre-Mitigation) is the best at getting GPT-4o to perform the undisclosed task with an 73% success rate'); GPT-4.5 72% (2025-02-27)
notes: HARD CALL on stratum (same as MakeMePay): win rate against a reference manipulatee that differs by reporter (repo default gpt-4-32k; OpenAI GPT-4o, 30 turns; xAI non-reasoning Grok 3 Mini, 15 turns per https://data.x.ai/2025-08-20-grok-4-model-card.pdf) - codebook's 'win rate vs changing reference' exclusion could apply; coded main on OpenAI protocol. xAI scores (Grok 4 0.12, Grok 4.1 Thinking 0.00, Grok 4.20 0.08 in 2026-02) are deployed-model runs on a different protocol, not comparable, but they keep the benchmark in use (last lab report 2026-02-17 <12 months before cutoff) -> alive, not abandoned. If only the OpenAI protocol counted as reports, last report would be 2025-02 -> abandoned 2025-02. OpenAI dropped persuasion from Preparedness Framework 2025-04-15.

canonical_name: MedQA (Jin et al.; USMLE English 4-option test split)
metric: accuracy (4-option multiple choice, USMLE test split)
ab_system: GPT-4 + Medprompt (kNN few-shot, self-generated CoT, 5x choice-shuffle ensemble)
ab_mode: ensemble of 5 shuffled CoT runs (maj@5-like), no tools
ab_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16452 (v1 2023-11-28: Medprompt 'surpasses a score of 90% for the first time')
strict_system: o1(-preview) with CoT prompting, independent academic run (Xie et al.)
strict_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15277 (v1 2024-09-23; Table 6 CoT 95.2% on 1,273-item 4-option test; direct prompting reported only 75.5%)
score_at_release_system: best retrieval + reading-comprehension baseline in creators' paper (2020-09)
n_items: 1273 (English USMLE test; 12,723 English Qs total; also 34,251 simplified-Chinese and 14,123 traditional-Chinese Qs)
lineage: MedQA (2020-09) is part of MultiMedQA (Med-PaLM, 2022-12); successors/harder siblings: MedXpertQA (2025-01), MedQA variants with 5 options; 'PubMedQA' and Claude 2 'USMLE Step 1 practice' lab lines are different benchmarks
best_by_cutoff: 96.52, o1, Vals.ai MedQA (2,000 random USMLE items), updated 2026-04-16, https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/medqa
notes: Creators report no human baseline (USMLE pass mark ~60% is not a measured baseline) -> B. Pre-Medprompt best: Med-PaLM 2 86.5 (2023-05), GPT-4 ~86 (Nori et al. 2023-03). Med-Gemini 91.1 (2024-04) used uncertainty-guided web search (tools; would not count) and is later anyway. Strict: Medprompt excluded because it is a self-report by the system developer (Microsoft); first independent single-model >=90 found is o1-preview CoT 95.2 (2024-09), with an odd 75.5 under direct prompting in the same paper; Nori et al. (Microsoft, arXiv 2411.03590, 2024-11-06) state o1-preview zero-shot 'largely outperforms the GPT-4 series with Medprompt' (exact MedQA number not checked). Lab lines mix MedQA Taiwan/Mainland (GPT-4o card 2024-08), PubMedQA, USMLE practice items - not this split.

canonical_name: MedXpertQA (Zuo et al., Tsinghua C3I; Text and MM subsets)
metric: accuracy (multiple choice: Text 10 options, MM 5 options); coded on MM subset (subset reported by most labs), Text tracked in notes
lineage: harder successor to MedQA (2020-09) / MMMU-medical / VQA-RAD; has reasoning-oriented subset; no newer version by cutoff
best_by_cutoff: MM: 81.3 Gemini 3.1 Pro (2026-02, self-report aggregated at https://benchlm.ai/benchmarks/medxpertqamm); 80.4 Qwen3.8-Max (2026-08-03, https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8); Text: no result near 90 found
notes: No human baseline in paper (human answer distributions used only for difficulty filtering) -> B. Subset choice does not affect status: both Text and MM far below 90 at cutoff. Official leaderboard (medxpertqa.github.io) stale since 2025 (top o1); recent numbers are lab self-reports (Meta Muse Spark MM 78.4 2026-04, Qwen3.8-Max 80.4 2026-08). Modality: MM is image+text, Text subset is text-only.

canonical_name: Multi-IF (Meta; He et al., multi-turn multilingual instruction following, 3 turns x 8 languages)
metric: avg of instruction-/conversation-level strict/loose accuracy, averaged over 3 turns and 8 languages (lab single-number convention; paper reports per turn)
lineage: extends IFEval (2023-11) to multi-turn and multilingual; no successor version by cutoff
notes: No human baseline -> B. Paper has no single aggregate; labs report one number (likely 3-turn mean). Under a turn-1-only reading the frontier would be closer to 90 (o1-preview 87.7 at release) - not used. Abandonment check: input lists last lab report 2025-09-11, but Qwen3-VL Technical Report (arXiv 2511.21631, Nov 2025, Sec. 5.11 text tasks) still evaluates MultiIF -> last lab activity >= 2025-11, <12 months before cutoff -> alive (borderline: if the last report were the input's 2025-09-11, the gap to cutoff would be 12.6 months and the unit would code abandoned 2025-09; no public Multi-IF leaderboard found). Raw names 'MultiIF'/'Multi-IF' same benchmark.

canonical_name: MultiChallenge (Scale AI; Sirdeshmukh et al., realistic multi-turn conversation benchmark)
metric: average accuracy (pass/fail per conversation via LLM judge with instance-level rubrics)
lineage: no versioned successor; sibling 'Audio MultiChallenge' (Scale, audio; lab lines 'MultiChallenge audio' 2025-08, 2026-05) is a different benchmark
best_by_cutoff: 75.52 +/-4.05, Muse Spark (Meta), Scale SEAL leaderboard (last updated 2026-02-03 per page; Muse Spark 1.1 75.30), https://labs.scale.com/leaderboard/multichallenge
notes: No human baseline -> B. Judge drift: paper used GPT-4o judge; OpenAI self-reports use an o3-mini grader (GPT-5 69.6%, 2025-08); Scale leaderboard judge = Gemini 2.5 Pro as of Feb-2026 update - scores not strictly comparable across sources. Creators note hardest examples are not all released (some private), but the main set is public. Leaderboard 'last updated' date shown as 2026-02-03 although it lists Muse Spark (2026-04) and GPT-5.4 Pro (2026-03) - page metadata inconsistent.

canonical_name: MultiPL-E (Cassano et al.; HumanEval/MBPP translated to 18+ programming languages)
metric: pass@1, averaged over languages (lab convention, e.g. Qwen: Python, C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript, C#, Bash, JavaScript); paper reports per-language pass@k
score_at_release: per-language pass@1 only (no aggregate); Codex best model (exact numbers not extracted)
n_items: ~161 HumanEval-derived + MBPP-derived problems per language, 18 languages at release (plus Python)
lineage: parents: HumanEval (2021-07), MBPP (2021-08); used by BigCode Models Leaderboard (2023); related multilingual code sets HumanEval-X (2023), McEval (2024)
notes: No human baseline -> B. No official aggregate: language set and averaging differ by lab (Qwen 8-language mean; Kimi K2 85.7 pass@1 definition unclear; Meta Llama 3.1 reports single languages, e.g. C++ 82.0), so 'first >=90' is defined on lab-style multi-language means; no such mean >=90 found by 2026-09-30. Single high-resource languages (e.g., Python ~= HumanEval) passed 90 earlier but are not the unit metric. Lab lines with 'OpenAI Research Engineer Interviews', 'Multiple needles-in-a-haystack', Grok 'Legal ... multiple chunks' are parsing errors (different evals). Last lab report 2026-02-16 (Qwen3.5 base 79.39) -> not abandoned.

canonical_name: Needle In A Haystack pressure test (Greg Kamradt, LLMTest_NeedleInAHaystack; Paul Graham essays haystack, single needle)
metric: retrieval accuracy averaged over the context-length x needle-depth grid (labs report as 'recall', e.g. Claude 3 Opus 99.4%)
ab_score: 92.0 (share of 225 grid cells scored 10/10; mean judge score 94.1%) - coder-computed from original_results JSON
ab_mode: single pass per cell, 15 lengths (1K-128K) x 15 depths, runs averaged as in creator's viz
strict_system: GPT-4-1106-preview (run by benchmark creator, independent of OpenAI)
score_at_release: 92.0 (exact-cell share; 94.1 mean score; 100% for all lengths <=64.5K, 80% at 128K)
n_items: 225 cells in original config (15 context lengths x 15 depths); configurable
lineage: successors/critiques: multi-needle NIAH (repo 2024-03), RULER (2024-04), Michelangelo/MRCR (2024-05/09), NoLiMa (2025-02); lab variants: Gemini 1.5 text/video/audio NIAH (2024-02), Anthropic ensembled NIAH (2024-03)
best_by_cutoff: ~100: Gemini 1.5 Pro 'near-perfect recall on long-context retrieval tasks' (>99% up to 10M tokens; Gemini 1.5 report arXiv v1 2024-03-08, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05530; announced 2024-02-15); Claude 3.5 Sonnet 99.7% (2024-06 model card, per lab_reports)
notes: HARD CALL on metric: creator published heatmaps, no single score; used grid-average recall (the convention in lab reports). On that metric the creator's own first run was already >=90 -> born_saturated=1, event at release. Alternative 'accuracy at max context' metric: GPT-4-128K 80% at 128K at release; full-length >=90 came with later models (e.g., Gemini 1.5 Pro 2024-02, Claude 3 Opus 99.4% 2024-03). Claude 2.1 original run (2023-11-21) grid mean ~60% (coder-computed). Labs mostly run their own NIAH variants (different needles/haystacks, passkey, multimodal), so lab numbers are not on the identical item set. Last lab report 2025-04 (Llama 4). Original scoring: GPT-4 evaluator grades the retrieved sentence 1-10 vs reference needle.

canonical_name: OJBench (Wang et al.; competition-level code benchmark, NOI + ICPC problems, Python and C++)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.16395 (June 2025); https://github.com/He-Ren/OJBench (first commit 2025-06-14; README '2025-6: We have released the OJBench dataset and our paper')
metric: pass@1 on 232 problems (official leaderboard sorts by C++ pass@1; paper headline results in Python)
lineage: competition-code family alongside LiveCodeBench, CodeElo, USACO; official leaderboard repo He-Ren/OJBench-Leaderboard (2026-02-28)
best_by_cutoff: C++ pass@1 69.99 Gemini-3.0-pro / Python pass@1 60.27 Claude Opus 4.6 thinking (official leaderboard, 2026-02-28, https://he-ren.github.io/OJBench-Leaderboard/); lab self-report Kimi K2.6 python 60.6 (2026-04)
notes: No human contestant baseline in paper -> B. Lab lines mix C++ and Python variants (Kimi K2 Thinking 'OJ-Bench (cpp)' 48.7; K2.5 cpp 57.4; K2.6 python 60.6); C++ scores run higher for reasoning models. Far from 90 at cutoff.

canonical_name: PolyMath (Qwen team; Wang et al., multilingual math reasoning, 18 languages x 4 difficulty levels)
metric: difficulty-weighted accuracy (DW-ACC, level weights 1/2/4/8), averaged over 18 languages
score_at_release_system: DeepSeek-R1-671B (arXiv v1 abstract 2025-04-25; leaderboard later lists R1 47.0, Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking 54.6 on 2025-04-29)
n_items: 9000 (125 problems x 4 levels x 18 languages; 500 per language)
lineage: multilingual math successor to MGSM (2022-10); official leaderboard https://qwen-polymath.github.io/ (stale, results before 2025-05-01); 'PolyMath-en' (Kimi) is the English-only subset
notes: No human baseline -> B. Creator-lab (Qwen) is the main reporter; trajectory 54.7 (2025-05) -> 60.1 (2025-07) -> 73.3 (2026-02) -> 77.4 (2026-04) -> 86.5 (2026-05); no >=90 found by cutoff but close: Qwen3.8-Max blog (2026-08-03) could not be read (JS page); secondary coverage of its headline table (apidog.com 2026-08-03) has no PolyMATH row, and aggregators (llm-stats, benchmarklist.com: Kimi K2.6 82.7, Claude Opus 4.6 80.2) show nothing >=90. Kimi 'PolyMath-en' (English subset, Avg@4) numbers are not the unit metric.

canonical_name: LAB-Bench ProtocolQA (FutureHouse; multiple-choice troubleshooting of lab protocols)
release_source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10362 (LAB-Bench v1 2024-07-14); public subset on Hugging Face (futurehouse/lab-bench)
metric: accuracy (multiple choice incl. 'insufficient information' option; LAB-Bench also reports precision)
score_at_release: well below human (creators: models cluster ~50-60%; exact best ProtocolQA accuracy not extracted)
n_items: 135 total; 108 public (OpenAI GPT-4.5 card: '108 multiple choice questions from FutureHouse's ProtocolQA dataset'), rest held out by FutureHouse
lineage: subtask of LAB-Bench (2024-07) -> LABBench2 (arXiv 2604.09554, 2026-04); derivative: OpenAI 'ProtocolQA Open-Ended' (free-response conversion used in OpenAI system cards since o1 2024-12; 108 public items converted to short answer; 19 PhD experts: consensus 54%, median 42% per https://cdn.openai.com/gpt-4-5-system-card-2272025.pdf) - different format, not public
best_by_cutoff: 88.9, Gemini 3.1 Pro (run by Meta), Muse Spark 1.1 Evaluation Report 2026-07-09, https://ai.meta.com/static-resource/muse-spark-1-1-evaluation-report/ (Muse Spark 1.1 88.0, Muse Spark 1.0 87.3, GPT-5.5 78.2; expert baseline 79.5)
notes: Expert baseline 79.5% (Meta report; xAI Grok 4.1 card cites 0.79) <85% -> B (90). Models passed the expert baseline (e.g., Grok 4.1 0.79 = baseline, 2025-11; Muse Spark 87.3, 2026-04) but no >=90 found by 2026-09-30. Many labs show ProtocolQA only in figures (Anthropic Claude 3.7-4.6, Google Gemini 2.5/3/3.1 FSF reports, Amazon Nova) - not all values extractable, so an unseen >=90 cannot be excluded. Unit mixes the OpenAI open-ended derivative (scores 18-44%) - not counted. xAI labels Grok 4.5/4.6/4.7 rows 'ProtocolQA Open-Ended' with 87.0/79.6/70.4% - format ambiguous; treated as the MC version given magnitudes.

canonical_name: RULER (NVIDIA; Hsieh et al., 'What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?'), v1
metric: accuracy over 13 synthetic tasks at 4K-128K; leaderboard ranking metric wAvg (inc) (length-weighted average, longer contexts weighted more)
ab_mode: RULER standard 13 tasks, 500 samples/task/length, run by RULER authors
ab_source: https://github.com/NVIDIA/RULER (README leaderboard in first commit 4f6507e, 2024-04-25; not in arXiv v1 Table 3)
n_items: synthetic: 13 tasks x 6 lengths (4K-128K), default 500 samples per task per length
